summary:
Backend and platform work on Vend's messaging platform - four Nordic marketplaces (finn.no, blocket.se, tori.fi, dba.dk) on one codebase, ~30 microservices on Kubernetes. The part I keep coming back to: changes that start in one brand and break in four, where no single team owns the fix. On FINN.no we redesigned the messaging frontend around the seller, with conversations grouped by ad, so a seller with several ads sees who is asking about what in one place. I built the backend changes behind it, worked through the design decisions with the team, and built parts of the frontend in React, TanStack and Tailwind.

Lately, prototyping LLM features inside the messaging thread.
Open banking under PSD2. Data-sharing APIs for Skatteetaten and Politi. Small team, end-to-end ownership, the kind of code review where the bar is set by the person asking the sharpest question.

Cards platform - global, millions of transactions a day. Led a team to ship a new microservice in two months. Ran a cloud infrastructure pilot on GCP + Pub/Sub, shelved by COVID budget cuts. Agile lead through the org's Atlassian migration.
Identity & access management (STIM), internal React + Spring app, GDPR document-redactor POC on Google Cloud OCR.

company: Tata Consultancy Services - Posten Norge / Bring
summary: Distributed Agile team building the logistics web platform for Posten Norge / Bring - 20+ Java web applications, 15–20 deploys a day, an in-house DevOps + monitoring framework we built because nothing off-the-shelf fit. A rotational posting from 2014 to 2019: a year in Oslo, then a year back in India, in turn. Test-code volume exceeded production-code volume, deliberately. Grew into team-lead responsibility. The high-cadence, delete-first engineering discipline I run on today started here.
Trained cohorts of 30–35 new joiners on core Java and J2EE. Teacher before I was an engineer.

Technical lead on a credit-rating platform for a European investment bank - functional analysis, technical design, code review, and deploys through SIT/UAT. Ran the sprint ceremonies alongside the build.

role: Technical Solutions Architect → Peoplesoft Functional Consultant
summary: Two years for the University of the Witwatersrand - a student admissions and progression rules engine, then a Peoplesoft Campus Solutions enrolments rollout. Grew from building the engine to owning the functional analysis on the platform side.

First job. Three years of Java/J2EE financial platforms for two clients - TATA Capital and AXIS Bank. Mutual funds, fixed deposits, vendor reference data, a trading-portal CMS - the origin of the financial-platform work. Started as a developer and moved through the ranks quickly, to technical architect and then technical lead, on the back-office and reconciliation systems.
